title: Derived balances, scaledTotalSupply()
detects: A token whose balances are not stored but computed. The contract keeps a scaled internal quantity per holder and multiplies it by a factor to produce the figure balanceOf returns, so this getter answering at all proves the accounting shape. What a wallet displays is derived, and it moves without any transfer taking place.
knownFalseNegative: This reads the accounting shape, not who moves the factor. On an Aave aToken the factor is the pool's liquidity index and moves with market interest; on AMPL it is set by a monetary-policy contract; a Token-2022 scaledUiAmountConfig mint has a literal authority who can set it at will, including future-dated. All three make the displayed number derived, which is what the transparency axis asks about, but only the last is a power one address holds. Reading this signal as 'someone can rewrite your balance' overstates the first two. A share-based token using a different getter reads absent: stETH is the case, and meta-share-balance reads it.

coversExamples.observed: scaledTotalSupply() answers the total gon supply; rebase(uint256,int256) is dispatched in the bytecode
scaledTotalSupply() answers; balanceOf multiplies the scaled balance by the pool's liquidity index

rationale: Before this pattern the transparency axis was unreadable on Ethereum: metadata-mutability was its only capability, no EVM pattern read it, and every Ethereum token reported the axis as n/a at 6 of 7 coverage. A scan of 52 Ethereum tokens found no contract exposing a name or symbol setter, so the Solana spelling of the capability has no Ethereum counterpart to read. The counterpart that does exist is the one Token-2022 calls scaledUiAmountConfig, already mapped to this capability on Solana: a balance that is computed from a factor rather than stored. Without this file the largest rebasing tokens on Ethereum report nothing on the axis that asks what a holder can check for themselves.
